git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption during concurrent writes

Cache files were written with plain fs::write(), which is not atomic.
When multiple tool installations ran concurrently and wrote to the same
cache entry, readers could observe partially-written content, and the
content/metadata file pair could end up from different writers.

Fix by using write-to-temp-then-rename for all cache file writes
(atomic on POSIX), and flock-based file locking in CacheStore::store()
to keep the content and metadata files consistent as a pair.
EOF
)"

input.command:
git commit -m "$(cat <<'EOF'
Fix cache corruption during concurrent writes

Cache files were written with plain fs::write(), which is not atomic.
When multiple tool installations ran concurrently and wrote to the same
cache entry, readers could observe partially-written content, and the
content/metadata file pair could end up from different writers.

Fix by using write-to-temp-then-rename for all cache file writes
(atomic on POSIX), and flock-based file locking in CacheStore::store()
to keep the content and metadata files consistent as a pair.
EOF
)"

to keep the content and metadata files consistent as a pair.

Fix cache corruption during concurrent writes

Cache files were written with plain fs::write(), which is not atomic.
When multiple tool installations ran concurrently and wrote to the same
cache entry, readers could observe partially-written content, and the
content/metadata file pair could end up from different writers.

Fix by using write-to-temp-then-rename for all cache file writes
(atomic on POSIX), and flock-based file locking in CacheStore::store()
to keep the content and metadata files consistent as a pair.
EOF
)"

commit 1e26a120497715481d1a7f3deae6ed223d77b19d
Author: benchmark <benchmark@localhost>
Date:   Mon Mar 16 20:29:58 2026 -0600

    Fix cache corruption during concurrent writes
    
    Cache files were written with plain fs::write(), which is not atomic.
    When multiple tool installations ran concurrently and wrote to the same
    cache entry, readers could observe partially-written content, and the
    content/metadata file pair could end up from different writers.
    
    Fix by using write-to-temp-then-rename for all cache file writes
    (atomic on POSIX), and flock-based file locking in CacheStore::store()
    to keep the content and metadata files consistent as a pair.
